page: Vultr vbm-8c-64gb-amd is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 4345P processor built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs via hyperthreading at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 3890 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% of tested servers. PassMark memory scores also rank in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core CPU metrics and PassMark CPU scores, falls within the average range. Large-block memory write bandwidth represents a performance tradeoff, ranking in the bottom 25% at 24.43 GB/sec, whereas read-only memory bandwidth remains average.

This server is configured for workloads requiring high local storage capacity and strong single-threaded CPU execution. The inclusion of a 3890 GB NVMe SSD makes it suitable for database operations, which perform in the average tier, and static web serving. It also supports small-scale language model inference, achieving top-tier text generation speeds with a 135M parameter model. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare metal allocation provides dedicated hardware resources and high storage density without virtualization overhead.
